record.summary: A 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and maintenance facility at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square, including the existing 4th & King Street Station itself. Owned by Prologis, with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP); Prologis has floated a development concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), anchored by a tower as tall as 850 feet (SF Standard, March 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path, the same one used for Pier 70, Mission Rock and Potrero Power Station.

notes.accuracy_caveat: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001, so its edges are recorded lot lines, not a trace. DataSF lists these four active lots (700 4th St, 311 Townsend St, an unaddressed lot, and 797 7th St) as the rail yard, and the earlier outline, built from the surrounding street centerlines, lies 83% inside them and is about 10 m wider along the long sides. The lots total about 16.7 acres, while SF Planning and Caltrain's FAQ describe a '20-acre site'; whether the planning site includes ground outside these lots, or the figure is rounded, is not settled. The lots are the legal boundaries; the 4th & King Street Station and the tracks are inside them. Status and use are as shown on this record.

changes.text: The March 2023 FAQ lists Fall 2022 as the expected start of public outreach; no source read dates the actual start. The Planning Department convened the Railyards Working Group from 2022 to 2024.
SF Railyards now uses real Assessor lot lines.

The record and an earlier timeline entry had said roughly 2,500 homes and up to 4 million square feet of commercial space; the SF Standard (March 10, 2026) says up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total, half commercial, with an 850-foot tower, and the January 2025 Chronicle article is now dated correctly. The 2022 outreach start is given as a year (the FAQ says fall 2022). The map notes now say DataSF has King St centerline segments from 6th to 7th St and that three active Assessor parcels lie inside the mapped area, correcting two earlier statements, and the inference that the site lies outside Mission Bay North was removed because DataSF's project-area layer puts about 41% of it inside 'Mission Bay - North'. The Board of Supervisors entry no longer names a district or supervisor.

changes.text: New adjacent record: the SF Railyards, a 20-acre active Caltrain rail yard and the 4th & King Street Station, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual operating easement, adjoining Mission Bay North. SF Planning is processing it as the "SF Railyards Planning Program" (Case No. 2023-000384CWP, per the January 2025 Planning Commission packet); Prologis has floated a concept of up to 2,500 housing units and about 8 million square feet in total (about half commercial), with an 850-foot tower (SF Standard, March 10, 2026); a Development Agreement is the expected approval path (SF Planning FAQ). The map shape is bounded by real street centerlines (Townsend, 4th, 7th, King), not a surveyed parcel; see the record's accuracy note. Pier & Point records the process and does not take a position.

open_questions: Whether Prologis's March 2026 submission constitutes a formal Preliminary Project Assessment/application distinct from the January 2025 informational Case No. 2023-000384CWP, or is still pre-application, is not confirmed here -- SF Planning's project page and hearing calendar are the places to check.

No named individual or group's public position on this specific project (for or against) has been found and sourced yet, distinct from the SF Railyards Working Group's general, collectively-summarized 'conceptual support' described in the January 2025 staff report.

The site's geometry is bounded by real street centerlines on three sides; the fourth (where King St's real centerline data ends short of 7th St, at the I-280 interchange) is a straight closing line, not a surveyed street -- see the shape's accuracy caveat.

As of 2026-09-29: the SF Chronicle article (January 8, 2025) reports the 850-foot tower concept but says it is too early to say how many units; the 2,500-unit and 8-million-sq-ft figures come from the SF Standard (March 10, 2026). The project page does not itself state the Development Agreement path, the FAQ does. Three active Assessor parcels lie inside this site's polygon (see the shape's accuracy caveat); whether this should be a real-parcel record is unresolved.

record.notes: The outline is the union of Assessor lots 8701004, 8701003, 3797004 and 8700001 (see the accuracy note). SF Planning Case No. 2023-000384CWP, 'SF Railyards Planning Program'. The 20-acre site at the nexus of SoMa, Mission Bay and Showplace Square: Caltrain's northern terminus and an active service/maintenance yard, owned by Prologis with Caltrain holding a perpetual easement to operate rail. A Development Agreement is the expected approval path (precedent: Pier 70, Mission Rock, Potrero Power Station, all DAs). Adjoins Mission Bay North. OCII's December 2019 Mission Bay Land Use Map, as seen in the map image (linked in this record's sources), labels N5A, N6 and N7 in this area with no land-use color and no drawn boundary, unlike the numbered Mission Bay North blocks beside it. That does not settle whether the site lies outside Mission Bay North: in DataSF's redevelopment project areas layer about 41% of this polygon lies inside 'Mission Bay - North', and parcels 8701003 and 8701004 are zoned MB-O. The map PDF and the project-area boundary have not yet been checked to settle this.
